scenario: The run of LLOG.15.3_literal_flip_admitted's program: [LLOG.15.3] "What its firing leaves is [LLOG.15.1]'s". A host `Politician(alice, honest: true)` makes `hope` emit `Hope(alice)`; `hope_live` reads it beside `ProbeHope(1)`. A `Bribe(alice)` then fires `corrupt` over that `Bribe` and `Hope`, which logs and emits `Politician logical name: "alice" honest: false`. That emit replaces the host `Politician` ([LFAC.2.5.3]), which ends `hope`'s match, so `Hope(alice)` loses its only justification and is retracted ([LLOG.15.1]), and with it `corrupt`'s own match ends inside its firing, at that emit. So the emitted `Politician(alice, false)` gains no justification and is retracted as it is made ([LLOG.15.1], [IRET.12.2]); nothing else holds it. Afterwards no `Politician` and no `Hope` is live, and the `Bribe` stays: `hope_live` beside `ProbeHope(2)` and `politician_live` beside `ProbePolitician(3)` would log a survivor, and `bribe_live` beside `ProbeBribe(4)` logs the `Bribe`. Each probe has its own pump, so no two rules fire in one pump. Expected: "hope alice at 1", "corrupt alice", "bribe alice at 4". Unlike LLOG.15.1_self_ending_match_justifies_nothing_after, the firing's match ends through the truth-maintenance cascade (`Hope` withdrawn), not through the emit replacing a fact the rule bound. PATH PINNED: libds's `ds_rete_terminal_justify` (rete/terminal.c) reading `firing_act_freed`, which `withdraw_justification`'s cascade sets when `Hope`'s retraction reaches `corrupt`'s terminal, from `eval_actions`' logical assert; the Mercury runtime's `ds.tms.activation_ended` noting the firing activation inside the action's settle, then `ds.tms.resolve_deferred` (`ds.exec.llog_15_1_justify_settled`). A runtime that entered the emit against `corrupt`'s ended activation keeps `Politician(alice, false)` live, and `politician_live` logs "politician alice at 3".
rules_ds:
schema Politician scope logical:
    name: String key
    honest: Bool mutable

schema Hope scope logical:
    name: String key

schema Bribe scope ttl 1_h:
    target: String

schema ProbeHope scope explicit:
    n: Int

schema ProbePolitician scope explicit:
    n: Int

schema ProbeBribe scope explicit:
    n: Int

rule hope:
    Politician p where p.honest == true
->
    emit Hope logical name: p.name

rule corrupt:
    Bribe b
    Hope h where h.name == b.target
->
    log info "corrupt {b.target}"
    emit Politician logical name: b.target honest: false

rule hope_live:
    ProbeHope q
    Hope h
->
    log info "hope {h.name} at {q.n}"

rule politician_live:
    ProbePolitician q
    Politician p
->
    log info "politician {p.name} at {q.n}"

rule bribe_live:
    ProbeBribe q
    Bribe b
->
    log info "bribe {b.target} at {q.n}"
